content.text:
User query:

Add a consistent retry policy to the TypeScript and Python SDKs. Specify retryable HTTP statuses (429 and 503), Retry-After handling, exponential backoff, maximum attempts and non-idempotent request protection in a new contracts/retry-policy.md before implementation. Implement and unit-test that contract in clients/typescript/client.ts and clients/python/client.py. Review both clients together and write reproducible conformance scenarios and results in tests/sdk-conformance.md, checking both use identical policy semantics. If that review finds nonconformance, request corrections to both client implementations and repeat the conformance review. Do not put retry behavior in the server or browser app.

arguments.name: contracts_retry_policy
arguments.task: Author contracts/retry-policy.md as the single authoritative retry spec for both SDKs. It must define: (1) retryable HTTP statuses 429 and 503 only; (2) Retry-After handling — honor the header when present and valid, supporting both delta-seconds and HTTP-date forms, otherwise fall back to backoff; (3) exponential backoff with a documented base delay, multiplier, cap and jitter rule; (4) maximum attempts (total tries including the first request) and what happens when exhausted; (5) non-idempotent request protection — which methods are safe to retry by default (e.g. GET/HEAD/OPTIONS and other idempotent methods), how POST/non-idempotent requests are excluded unless the caller opts in, and the opt-in mechanism; (6) error/exception surfaced after final failure. Include a short semantics table so TS and Python implementations can be compared point-by-point. Do not change any code. Deliverable: contracts/retry-policy.md exists with all sections above.

arguments.name: ts_client_retry
arguments.task: Implement the retry policy defined in contracts/retry-policy.md inside clients/typescript/client.ts (the TypeScript SDK client). Requirements: retry only on statuses 429 and 503; honor Retry-After (delta-seconds and HTTP-date) when present and valid, otherwise use the contract's exponential backoff (base, multiplier, cap, jitter); enforce the contract's maximum attempts and surface the contract's terminal failure error; never retry non-idempotent requests unless the caller explicitly opts in via the contract's opt-in mechanism. Keep changes confined to the TypeScript client (plus its own local helper/type files if strictly necessary). Do NOT add retry behavior to the server or the browser app, and do NOT edit clients/python/* or contracts/retry-policy.md. Also add unit tests in the TypeScript test location that assert each contract clause: 429 retried, 503 retried, other 4xx/5xx not retried, Retry-After seconds honored, Retry-After date honored, backoff growth/cap, max attempts exhaustion error, non-idempotent blocked by default and allowed with opt-in. Deliverable: contract implemented in clients/typescript/client.ts and unit tests pass.

arguments.name: py_client_retry
arguments.task: Implement the retry policy defined in contracts/retry-policy.md inside clients/python/client.py (the Python SDK client). Requirements: retry only on statuses 429 and 503; honor Retry-After (delta-seconds and HTTP-date) when present and valid, otherwise use the contract's exponential backoff (base, multiplier, cap, jitter); enforce the contract's maximum attempts and raise the contract's terminal failure error; never retry non-idempotent requests unless the caller explicitly opts in via the contract's opt-in mechanism. Semantics must match the TypeScript client exactly (same status set, same defaults, same precedence of Retry-After over backoff, same attempt counting, same idempotency gate). Keep changes confined to clients/python/client.py (plus its own local helper module if strictly necessary). Do NOT add retry behavior to the server or the browser app, and do NOT edit clients/typescript/* or contracts/retry-policy.md. Also add unit tests in the Python test location asserting each contract clause: 429 retried, 503 retried, other 4xx/5xx not retried, Retry-After seconds honored, Retry-After date honored, backoff growth/cap, max attempts exhaustion error, non-idempotent blocked by default and allowed with opt-in. Deliverable: contract implemented in clients/python/client.py and unit tests pass.

arguments.name: sdk_conformance_review
arguments.task: Review the TypeScript and Python SDK retry implementations together for semantic conformance to contracts/retry-policy.md. Read clients/typescript/client.ts, clients/python/client.py and their unit tests, then write tests/sdk-conformance.md containing reproducible conformance scenarios (given/when/then with concrete inputs: status codes 429/503/other 4xx-5xx, Retry-After seconds and HTTP-date values, attempt counts, request methods) plus a results table recording each scenario's observed behavior in BOTH clients and whether they match. Check point-by-point: identical retryable status set, identical Retry-After precedence and parsing, identical backoff base/multiplier/cap/jitter rule, identical maximum-attempt counting and terminal error, identical non-idempotent gate and opt-in mechanism, and confirm no retry logic leaked into the server or browser app. The file must let a later reader rerun every scenario. Deliverable: tests/sdk-conformance.md written with all scenarios and results.

content.text:
The plan is complete: contract authored first, both SDK clients implemented in parallel against it, then a joint conformance review that can loop corrections back into either client.


```
contracts/retry-policy.md  (single source of truth)
        |
        +--> clients/typescript/client.ts  + unit tests  --+
        |                                                 |
        +--> clients/python/client.py     + unit tests  --+--> tests/sdk-conformance.md
                                                          |
                          feedback: nonconformance -> correct both clients, rerun review
```

- **contracts_retry_policy** — root node writing the spec: retryable statuses limited to 429/503, Retry-After precedence (delta-seconds and HTTP-date), exponential backoff base/multiplier/cap/jitter, max attempts and terminal error, non-idempotent gate plus explicit opt-in, and a semantics table for cross-language comparison.
- **ts_client_retry / py_client_retry** — independent parallel implementers, each confined to its own client file plus its own unit tests, with an explicit prohibition on touching the other language, the contract, or adding retry logic to the server/browser app.
- **sdk_conformance_review** — depends on both clients; writes reproducible given/when/then scenarios and a two-column results table proving identical semantics, and verifies no retry behavior leaked outside the SDKs.
- **Feedback edges** — reviewer routes back to *both* client owners when scenarios diverge, so corrections are applied symmetrically and the conformance doc is regenerated rather than patched one-sidedly.
